questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Shalini was scrolling down the phone screen while waiting for her friend.

B. Her friend brought a bouquet for Shalini from the market place.

C. When her friend arrived, they went to the market place.

D. The market place was thronging with people.
questions.solution:
The correct order is ACDB.

Sentence A comes first as it introduces us to the main subject of the passage (Shalini). In the rest of the sentences, the subject is referred to by using pronouns. Sentence C states that she, along with her friend, went to the market. The other two sentences, D and B, talk about the events after they arrived at the market. Therefore, C follows A. So, among the given options, option (d) is the correct answer.

A is the first part of the sentence. P follows A as it conveys the field of the 2007- 2009 Study. Q follows P as it talks about the purpose of the techniques. Q ends with the adjective 'deep' which requires a noun after it. Sentence R starts with the noun 'space'. So, R can follow Q. The remaining part S is the last part of the sentence.

The correct sentence is: A 2007-2009 study explored forward thinking techniques to synchronise time on board deep space probes for accurate navigation, in particular looking into low-cost options.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. The indentured labourers fix the roads.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

The indentured labourers fix the roads.

options.text: The roads was fixed by indentured labourers.
options.html: The roads was fixed by indentured labourers.

options.text: The roads were fixed by indentured labourers.
options.html: The roads were fixed by indentured labourers.

options.text: The roads are fixed by indentured labourers.
options.html: The roads are fixed by indentured labourers.

options.text: The roads were being fixed by indentured labourers.
options.html: The roads were being fixed by indentured labourers.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Present Indefinite. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Present Indefinite.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + V1/V5 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

She likes you. (Active Voice)

You are liked by her. (Passive Voice)

The options except (c) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (c): The roads are fixed by indentured labourers.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb ['was' in the given sentence] and preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Past Indefinite. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Past Indefinite.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject ['Gandolf, the savior'] + V2 ['defeated'] + Object ['evil king'].

For example:

The Champions League was won by Real Madrid. (Passive Voice)

Real Madrid won the Champions League. (Active Voice)

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a): Gandolf, the savior, defeated the evil king.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The manager told her that / she should be a bit more / careful while executed the / orders of the company.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech. He said, 'Let us wait for the award'.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

He said, 'Let us wait for the award'.

options.html: He proposed that they should wait for the award.

options.text: He said that he should wait for the award.
options.html: He said that he should wait for the award.

options.text: He proposed that he should wait for the award.
options.html: He proposed that he should wait for the award.

options.text: He said that they should waited for the award.
options.html: He said that they should waited for the award.

questions.solution:
Option (a) is the correct answer.

"Let" is used to mean "to allow" (request) or "to propose/suggest".

"Let" as a proposal/suggestion:

Rules to follow:

"Said/said to" is changed to "proposed/proposed to" or "suggested/suggested to"

That is added in indirect speech.

"Let" is removed in the indirect speech.

Modal verb "should" is added in indirect speech.

Pronouns are changed accordingly.

Example 1: He said, "Let us go to the amusement park." (Direct Speech)

He suggested that they should go to the amusement park. (Indirect Speech)

Example 2: I said to him, "Let us attend the office party." (Direct Speech)

I proposed to him that we should attend the office party. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

The reporting verb 'said' is changed into 'proposed'.

Inverted commas is removed and 'that' is introduced.

The pronoun 'us' is changed into 'they'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a): He proposed that they should wait for the award.

questions.question: Select the correct direct form of the given sentence. Leena said that his relatives were landing the next day.
questions.questionHtml:

questions.solution:
Option (d) is the correct answer.

The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Present Continuous Tense.

Past Continuous (Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object) will be converted into Present Continuous (Subject + is/am/are + V1 +ing + Object)

For example:

He said that he was checking the assignment. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I am checking the assignment." (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

'That' is removed and inverted commas are added.

The verb 'were landing' (simple past continuous) is changed into 'are landing' (simple present continuous).

'The next day' is changed into 'tomorrow'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (d): Leena said, "His relatives are landing tomorrow."
